significance.justification: Verified true, the conclusion would be that the base-model quantities in the “EM-susceptibility fingerprint” predict post-fine-tuning misalignment across datasets, while experimentally changing “the base-model coupling between the task update and the misalignment direction” changes EM magnitude; this is primarily a form-(iii) predictive coupling and dose-response law, reinforced by a form-(ii) causal mechanism. It would establish both a consequential phenomenon—risk can be forecast before fine-tuning—and a mechanism fixing expectations for unseen datasets and explaining why orthogonalizing or enhancing the coupling should respectively lower or raise EM, directly addressing the dataset- and training-dependent behavior documented by Betley et al., “Emergent Misalignment: Narrow finetuning can produce broadly misaligned LLMs” (2025, arXiv:2502.17424). Verified false across the asserted model-family and recipe scope would distinguish a dynamics-dependent world from one governed by static base geometry, although it would not justify the broad statement that researchers should entirely “stop seeking static pre-training geometry predictors”; true and false are nevertheless determinate because they imply opposing predictive and causal relations. Topic-substitution check: replacing these specific coupling, forecasting, and pre-conditioning claims with generic mechanistic LLM-safety language would not retain this score—the cross-dataset predictive law and causal dose-response are materially more constraining than the topic’s median direction-plus-steering hypothesis.

reach.justification: The claim names two concrete handles: the “EM-susceptibility fingerprint” and a “one-time, dataset-agnostic Pre-Conditioning edit”; the former is explicitly ex ante because it acts “before a single practitioner gradient step,” enabling dataset screening or curation with an action window, while the latter is a preventive model-shipping intervention. Although “directions, fingerprints, and edits are model-family-specific and require re-extraction,” the substantive hypothesis is a transferable relation—greater projection/update coupling predicts greater EM—so recalibration on another model should recover a predicted coupling-risk relationship rather than merely provide an open-ended search procedure. Its asserted scope covers several model families and a bank of later fine-tunes, with downstream uptake by “a fine-tuning platform or safety team,” but it expressly does not guarantee alignment for arbitrary fine-tunes and may depend on training recipe, preventing 9–10 reach. Topic-substitution check: generic interpretability for LLM safety would not itself supply an ex-ante dataset gate or pre-conditioned base model, so the reach score comes from these claim-specific handles rather than from the importance of the safety topic.
